\begin{hbdefinition}{def:p02-arbitrary-prop-language}{Finitary propositional language on an arbitrary set}
For an arbitrary set \(P\), \(\operatorname{Form}(P)\) is the least set
containing \(P\) and closed under the fixed finitary connectives. A valuation
is a total function \(v:P\to\{0,1\}\), extended by structural recursion. The
word ``arbitrary'' is necessary because the source completeness proof
enumerates a countable alphabet. This stands as a set-indexed syntax/semantics,
differs only in cardinality rather than formula arity, and is used in the
choice-calibrated completeness theorem.  Write
\(\Gamma\vdash_{\mathsf{CPL}(P)}\varphi\) when there is a finite
discharge-labelled natural-deduction tree using exactly the inherited
\(\mathsf{ND}_{\mathsf{CPL}}\) rules, with formula metavariables ranging over
\(\operatorname{Form}(P)\) and every open assumption belonging to \(\Gamma\

\(L\) as \(L\lor L\).  The instance
is satisfiable iff no occurring variable \(p\) has both \(p\) and \(\neg p\)
in one strongly connected component.  The test runs in \(O(N)\) time.
\end{hbtheorem}

\begin{hbtheorem}{thm:p02-xor-sat}{cited=Schaefer1978}{XOR-SAT tractability}
XOR satisfiability is decidable by Gaussian elimination over the two-element
field, for example in \(O(mn\min\{m,n\})\) field operations with a dense
implementation.
\end{hbtheorem}

\begin{hbtheorem}{thm:p02-propositional-duality}{proved=annex:p2.1.8}{Duality theorem}
Let \(\bar v(p)=1-v(p)\).  For every NNF presentation \(\alpha\),
\[
 v\entails\alpha^{\mathrm d}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \bar v\not\entails\alpha.
\]
Consequently dualization is an involution, preserves logical equivalence,
exchanges valid formulas with unsatisfiable formulas, and exchanges CNF with
DNF.
\end{hbtheorem}

\begin{annexitem}{annex:p2.1.8}{thm:p02-propositional-duality}{Duality theorem}
\begin{proof}
Induct on the displayed NNF presentation \(\alpha\).  If \(\alpha\) is a
positive literal \(p\), then
\(v\entails p\) iff \(\bar v\not\entails p\).  If it is \(\neg p\), then
\(v\entails\neg p\) iff \(v(p)=0\), iff
\(\bar v(p)=1\), iff \(\bar v\not\entails\neg p\).  The two unit
cases follow from \(\bottom^{\mathrm d}=\topv\) and
\(\topv^{\mathrm d}=\bottom\).  For conjunction,
\[
 v\entails(\beta\land\gamma)^{\mathrm d}
 \quad\text{iff}\quad
 v\entails\beta^{\mathrm d}\text{ or }v\entails\gamma^{\mathrm d}
 \quad\text{iff}\quad
 \bar v\not\entails\beta\land\gamma,
\]
by the induction hypotheses; the disjunction case is dual.  This proves the
displayed semantic identity.

The recursive clauses also give \((\alpha^{\mathrm d})^{\mathrm d}=\alpha\)
by structural induction.  If \(\alpha\Leftrightarrow\beta\), apply the
semantic identity to \(\bar v\) for each \(v\) to obtain
\(\alpha^{\mathrm d}\Leftrightarrow\beta^{\mathrm d}\); the converse follows
from involution.  If \(\alpha\) is valid, the identity makes
\(\alpha^{\mathrm d}\) false under every \(v\).  Conversely, if the dual is
unsatisfiable, apply the identity with \(v=\bar u\) to show that every \(u\)
satisfies \(\alpha\).  Finally, the syntactic clauses swap every outer
conjunction with disjunction, every clause-disjunction with a conjunction of
the same literals, and the two empty units; hence they exchange CNF and DNF.
\end{proof}
\end{annexitem}

\section{Normal forms}
\label{sec:prop-syntax-semantics-04}

\begin{definition}[Propositional literal, clause, and formula interpretation]
A \emph{propositional literal} is a propositional variable or the negation of
a propositional variable.  A \emph{clause} is a finite set of propositional
literals.  Thus clause equality is set equality: order and repeated
occurrences are not part of a clause.

To map this set object back to the formula language, put
\[
 \operatorname{code}(p_n)=2n,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{code}(\neg p_n)=2n+1.
\]
For a clause \(C\), let \(k=\abs{C}\); when \(k>0\), list its members as
\(L_1,\ldots,L_k\) in strictly increasing code order and define, by downward
recursion,
\[
 D_k\defeq L_k,
 \qquad
 D_i\defeq(L_i\lor D_{i+1})\quad(1\leq i<k).
\]
Then define
\[
 \operatorname{form}_{\CPL}(C)\defeq
 \begin{cases}
  \bottom,&C=\varnothing,\\
  D_1,&C\ne\varnothing.
 \end{cases}
\]
This is an exact metalinguistic function from clauses to
\(\Fm_{\CPL}\), not a new formula constructor.  A valuation \(v\)
\emph{satisfies} \(C\) iff
\(v\entails\operatorname{form}_{\CPL}(C)\).  In particular, the empty
clause is false under every valuation.
\end{definition}

\section{Equivalence and equisatisfiability}
\label{sec:automated-reasoning-02}

\begin{definition}[Equisatisfiability]
Formulas \(\varphi\) and \(\psi\), possibly in different signatures, are
\emph{equisatisfiable} iff the two formulas are either both satisfiable
or both unsatisfiable.
\end{definition}

Logical equivalence is stronger: it compares truth under corresponding
valuations, whereas equisatisfiability compares only existence of a satisfying
valuation.  Tseitin clausification \cite{Tseitin1968} introduces a fresh
variable for each
selected subformula and constrains that variable to have the same truth value
as the subformula.  If \(p_\varphi\) names the complete input formula
\(\varphi\), the output also contains the unit clause \(\set{p_\varphi}\),
which requires the root variable to be true.  Call the resulting finite clause
set \(S_\varphi\).  The conjunction of the
\(\operatorname{form}_{\CPL}\)-images in any enumeration of
\(S_\varphi\) is equisatisfiable with \(\varphi\) in the expanded signature,
and
\(S_\varphi\) can have size linear in the size of \(\varphi\).  The output is
not literally the same formula and need not be logically equivalent in the
original signature.

  S_\theta=
  \set{
    \set{\neg p_\theta,P},
    \set{\neg p_\theta,Q},
    \set{p_\theta,\neg P,\neg Q}
  }.
\]

\begin{hbdefinition}{def:p02-equisatisfiability}{Equisatisfiability}
Two formulas, possibly over different variable sets, are
\emph{equisatisfiable} iff either both are satisfiable or both are
unsatisfiable.  This is a metalinguistic relation between formulas and is
strictly weaker than logical equivalence when fresh variables are introduced.
\end{hbdefinition}

\begin{hbtheorem}{thm:p02-tseitin}{cited=Prestwich2021}{Tseitin transformation}
For every formula \(\varphi\), a linear-time transformation produces a CNF
formula \(T_\varphi\) of linear size over the original variables and fresh
auxiliary variables such that, for every valuation \(v\) of the original
variables,
\[
 v\entails\varphi
 \quad\text{iff}\quad
 \text{there is a unique extension }w\supseteq v
 \text{ with }w\entails T_\varphi.
\]
The uniqueness is for the full biconditional definitional constraints.  Thus
\(T_\varphi\) is equisatisfiable with \(\varphi\), but is not a
same-vocabulary logically equivalent formula.  The historical construction is
due to Tseitin~\cite{Tseitin1968}; the Part~12 automation entry gives the gate
constraints and worked construction.  This is depth row D-P2-007.
\end{hbtheorem}
